guides.why: The oil lubricates the engine, clutch and gearbox and carries most of the heat. There is under a litre of it, so it wears out quickly.
guides.when: 1,000 km, then every 6,000 km, and at least once a year.
tools: Socket for the drain bolt (12 mm thread)

parts.name: Engine oil SAE 10W-30, JASO MA, API SJ or higher
parts.qty: 0.8 L (0.85 L with a filter change)
parts.note: Not oils marked Energy Conserving or Resource Conserving

steps: Put the bike on its centerstand on level ground. Warm the engine so the oil drains fully.
Remove the drain bolt and sealing washer and drain the oil completely.
Fit the drain bolt with a new sealing washer and tighten to 24 N·m.
Fill with 0.8 L of oil, or 0.85 L if the oil filter was changed. Check the filler cap O-ring and replace it if damaged.
Idle for 3–5 minutes, stop, wait 2–3 minutes, then read the dipstick without screwing it in. The level must sit between the upper and lower marks.
checks: 0.8 L after draining, 0.85 L after draining and filter change, 1.0 L after disassembly (2-18)
pitfalls: The drain bolt threads into the aluminium case: use a torque wrench.
Read the dipstick resting on the threads, not screwed in.

guides.time: Adds 10 min to an oil change
guides.why: This engine has a paper cartridge oil filter behind a small cover on the right side, in addition to the strainer screen and centrifugal filter.
guides.when: Replace at 12,000, 24,000 and 36,000 km, with the oil.
tools: Socket for the two cover bolts

parts.name: O-ring, 39.8 × 2.2
parts.note: The filter cover O-ring, new and oiled

steps: Drain the engine oil.
Remove the two bolts, the filter cover, O-ring, spring and filter.
Fit the new filter with its "OUT-SIDE" mark facing out, toward the cover.
Refit the spring and cover with a new oiled O-ring.
Refill with 0.85 L of oil and check the level.
checks: 0.85 L after draining and filter change (2-18)
pitfalls: A filter fitted backwards will cause severe engine damage. The "OUT-SIDE" mark faces out.

guides.why: Valve clearance closes up as the seats wear. Too little can stop a valve sealing and burn it; too much is noisy and costs power.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km. Engine cold, below 35 °C.
steps: Remove the valve adjusting hole caps, the timing hole cap and the crankshaft hole cap.
Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise until the "T" mark on the flywheel lines up with the index notch on the left crankcase cover.
Check the piston is at TDC on the compression stroke: both rocker arms have slack. If not, turn the crankshaft one more full turn and realign the "T" mark.
Measure between the adjusting screw and the valve stem: IN 0.08 ± 0.02 mm, EX 0.20 ± 0.02 mm.
To adjust, loosen the lock nut, turn the screw until the gauge drags lightly, hold the screw and tighten the lock nut to 9.0 N·m with oiled threads. Recheck.
Refit the caps with new O-rings: timing hole cap 6.0 N·m, crankshaft hole cap 8.0 N·m.
checks: Lock nut 9.0 N·m, timing hole cap 6.0 N·m, crankshaft hole cap 8.0 N·m (1-13)
pitfalls: Measuring on the exhaust stroke instead of compression TDC.
The clearance tightens slightly as the lock nut is tightened: always recheck.

guides.why: A worn plug causes hard starting, misfires and lost power.
guides.when: Inspect at 6,000, 18,000 and 30,000 km; replace at 12,000, 24,000 and 36,000 km.
tools: Spark plug wrench from the tool kit (89216-KPP-900), or a 16 mm thin-wall plug socket
steps: Pull the plug cap off and clean around the plug so dirt cannot fall into the cylinder.
Remove the plug and inspect the electrodes and insulator.
Set the gap to 0.8–0.9 mm.
Start the plug by hand, then tighten to 16 N·m.
pitfalls: Cross-threading the aluminium head: always start the plug by hand.

guides.why: A mesh screen in the bottom of the crankcase catches debris before it reaches the oil pump. It sits behind the right crankcase cover, so clean it with the centrifugal filter.
guides.when: Clean at 12,000, 24,000 and 36,000 km. Honda recommends a dealer (**).

parts.name: Gasket, R. crankcase cover
parts.note: New whenever the cover comes off

parts.name: Screen, oil filter
parts.note: Normally cleaned and reused; replace if torn

steps: Drain the engine oil completely.
Remove the step bar and the exhaust pipe/muffler.
Loosen the right crankcase cover bolts in a crisscross pattern in several steps and remove the cover.
Pull the oil strainer screen out with pliers, clean it and dry it.
Refit the screen with its tapered side facing the crankcase and the thinner edge up.
Do the centrifugal filter now, while the cover is off.
Fit a new cover gasket. Align the clutch adjuster boss with the hole in the cover, and the punch mark on the clutch lever with the index line on the gearshift spindle.
Check the kickstarter spindle oil seal; replace it if damaged.
Refill with oil, then adjust the clutch: the adjusting screw setting is 1/8 turn clockwise.
checks: Right crankcase cover protector bolts 12 N·m (1-14)
Clutch adjusting screw lock nut 12 N·m (1-14)
pitfalls: Forgetting to adjust the clutch after refitting the cover.
Fitting the screen backwards: the tapered side goes toward the crankcase.

videos.title: Honda Super Cub Oil Spinner and Filter Screen Service Part 2
videos.note: Super Cub C125: same engine family

guides.time: Adds 20 min to the strainer screen job
guides.why: A spinning drum on the crankshaft throws heavy particles outward into a sludge layer. Left uncleaned, the sludge can block the oil flow.
guides.when: Clean at 12,000, 24,000 and 36,000 km. Honda recommends a dealer (**).
steps: Drain the oil and remove the right crankcase cover.
Remove the 3 bolts and the centrifugal filter cover from the drive plate.
Clean the filter cover and the inside of the drive plate.
Fit a new gasket with its ledged side facing the filter cover.
Apply locking agent to the 3 bolts (a 4.0 mm band, leaving 1.6 mm at the tip clean) and tighten to 5.0 N·m.
Refit the right cover, refill the oil and adjust the clutch.
checks: Filter cover bolts 5.0 N·m with locking agent (1-13)
pitfalls: 5 N·m is very light. Use an inch-pound torque wrench; the bolts strip easily.

videos.title: Honda Supercub 8000 Mile oil spinner service
Motorcycle Centrifugal Oil Filter CLEANING Explained

guides.why: The element is a viscous (oil-wetted) paper type. It cannot be cleaned; blowing it out with air ruins it.
guides.when: Replace at 18,000 and 36,000 km, more often in dust or wet riding.
tools: Torque driver (1.1 N·m) or careful hands
steps: Remove the left main pipe side cover.
Remove the air cleaner housing cover screws and the cover.
Remove the element; wipe dirt or water out of the housing.
Fit the new element, refit the cover and tighten the screws to 1.1 N·m.
pitfalls: Over-tightening the plastic cover screws strips them.

videos.title: Honda CT125 Trail 125 How to Replace the Air Filter

guides.why: Blow-by gas goes from the crankcase into the air box. Oil and water collect in a drain tube at the bottom of the air cleaner housing.
guides.when: Every 6,000 km, and more often in rain or at full throttle.
steps: Find the drain plug at the bottom of the air cleaner housing.
Remove the plug, drain the deposits into a container and refit.
pitfalls: A full drain tube can push oil into the air filter.

guides.why: The fuel feed hose runs from the in-tank pump to the injector with quick-connect fittings. A leak is a fire risk.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly (*).
steps: Check the fuel feed hose for cracks, kinks, chafing and fuel smell.
Check both quick-connect fittings are locked.
Before disconnecting anything, relieve the fuel pressure as the manual describes.
checks: Fuel pump flow 82 cm³ minimum per 10 s at 12 V (1-7)
pitfalls: Bending or twisting the resin hose damages it.

guides.why: A sticking throttle is dangerous; too little free play can raise the idle when you turn the bars.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly (*).
steps: Engine off: turn the bars lock to lock and check the grip opens and snaps closed in every position.
Measure the free play at the grip flange: 2–6 mm.
Adjust at the throttle cable adjuster and tighten the lock nuts.
checks: Handlebar-side cable lock nuts 3.0 N·m, adjust nut 3.8 N·m (1-15)
pitfalls: Routing added switches or cables where they pinch the throttle cables.

guides.why: Idle speed is set by the ECM; on Indonesian and Thai bikes the idle air screw sets the base opening.
guides.when: Inspect at every service (*).
steps: Warm the engine and let it idle: 1,400 ± 100 rpm.
Idle air screw standard opening: 1-7/8 turns out from fully seated (Indonesia, Thailand).
After throttle body work, do the TP sensor reset.
pitfalls: Adjusting idle on a cold engine.

guides.why: A dry or badly adjusted chain wears itself and both sprockets quickly.
guides.when: Inspect and lubricate every 500 km.

parts.name: Chain, drive (DID428HDS3-108RB)
parts.note: Only if worn past its limit or kinked

parts.name: Slider, chain
parts.note: Only if grooved or worn thin

steps: Put the bike on the centerstand, gearbox in neutral, engine off.
Measure slack midway between the sprockets: 25–35 mm, limit 50 mm.
To adjust, loosen the rear axle nut, turn both adjusters equally, then tighten the axle nut to 59 N·m.
Clean and lubricate the chain.
pitfalls: Adjusting the two sides unevenly, which misaligns the wheel.

guides.time: 10 min to check, 1 h to replace
guides.why: Brake fluid absorbs water over time, which lowers its boiling point and corrodes the system.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km; replace every 2 years.
tools: Clear bleeder hose and catch bottle
8 mm wrench for the bleed valves

parts.name: DOT 3 or DOT 4 brake fluid, sealed container
parts.note: Only if low, or for the 2-year replacement

steps: With the bike upright, check the fluid level in the front and rear reservoirs.
A falling level usually means worn pads; check them before topping up.
Replacement and bleeding follow the Basic Shop Manual. Bleed valves 5.4 N·m.
checks: Bleed valves 5.4 N·m, reservoir cap screws 1.5 N·m (1-15, 1-16)
pitfalls: Brake fluid strips paint; cover the tank and plastics.

videos.title: COMPLETE brake flush w/ ABS bleeding - Honda
videos.note: Honda with ABS, not a CT125

guides.why: Pads worn to the backing plate ruin the disc and stop poorly.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly.

parts.name: Pad set, front
parts.note: Only if worn to the wear grooves

parts.name: Pad set, rear
parts.note: Only if worn to the wear grooves

steps: Look at the pads from behind the caliper; replace both pads in a caliper if either is worn to the grooves.
Front pad replacement: hanger pin 17 N·m, caliper mounting bolts 30 N·m (new bolts).
Rear pad replacement.
checks: Front disc 3.3–3.7 mm, limit 3.0 mm; rear 3.8–4.2 mm, limit 3.5 mm (1-10)
pitfalls: Pushing the pistons back with the reservoir full overflows it.

guides.why: A leak, a damaged hose or a spongy lever means the brakes may not work when needed.
guides.when: Inspect at every service and yearly.
steps: Check the lever and pedal feel; neither should be spongy.
Check hoses, oil bolts and fittings for leaks, cracks and chafing.
Check the ABS brake pipe joints.

guides.why: The brake light must come on as soon as either brake starts to work.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly.
steps: Ignition on: check the brake light comes on with the lever and with the pedal, just before the brake engages.
checks: Front brake light switch screw 1.2 N·m (1-15)

videos.title: How to Adjust Honda Trail 125 Brake Pedal Light Sensor

guides.why: A low beam aimed too high dazzles oncoming traffic; too low and you outride it.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly.
steps: Adjust the beam vertically with the adjusting bolt.

guides.why: An automatic centrifugal clutch with a manual clutch behind it; a badly adjusted clutch slips or drags and shifts poorly.
guides.when: Inspect at every service and yearly (*).
steps: Loosen the clutch adjusting screw lock nut on the right crankcase cover.
Turn the adjusting screw to its specified setting, 1/8 turn clockwise, as the manual describes.
Hold the screw and tighten the lock nut to 12 N·m. Test the shift feel.
checks: Clutch adjusting screw lock nut 12 N·m (1-14)

videos.title: Honda CT 125/Trail 125 4 Month Review - Clutch Explained

guides.why: A weak spring lets the stand drop while riding.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly.
steps: Check the spring for damage and that the stand moves freely and snaps up.
Korea: check the sidestand switch stops the engine with the stand down and in gear.
checks: Pivot bolt 18 N·m, pivot nut 44 N·m (1-14)

guides.why: Leaking fork seals and worn shocks hurt braking and handling.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly (*).

parts.name: Seal set, fr. fork
parts.note: Only if a fork leg leaks; 1 per leg

steps: Pump the forks with the front brake on; check for leaks and smooth action.
Check the rear shocks for leaks and the mounts for play.
Fork oil, if replacing: 10W, 120 ± 2.5 cm³ per leg, level 140 mm.
checks: Shock mounts 44 / 29 N·m, swingarm pivot 54 N·m (1-15)

guides.why: Vibration loosens fasteners.
guides.when: At 1,000 km, then every 12,000 km and yearly (*).
steps: Check the specified torques for the main fasteners.
Anything not listed takes the standard torque for its thread size.

videos.title: EVERY TORQUE VALUE for EVERY FASTENER on the Honda Trail 125 - CT125 gets a new spark plug!

guides.why: Tire pressure and spoke tension decide how the bike grips and how long the rims last.
guides.when: Inspect every 6,000 km and yearly (**).
steps: Set cold pressures: front 175 kPa, rear 225 kPa (rider only).
Check tread, cuts and the spokes; tighten loose spokes.
Check wheel bearings for play.
checks: Front 175 kPa, rear 225 kPa; Korea rear with passenger 280 kPa (1-10)

videos.title: How To Change The Front Tire On Your Honda Trail 125 Motorcycle
2020 Honda CT125 Hunter Cub Trail - Big Off-Road Tyre Change!

guides.why: Loose or notchy bearings make the steering wander or stick.
guides.when: Inspect at 12,000, 24,000 and 36,000 km and yearly (**).
steps: With the front wheel off the ground, turn the bars lock to lock; they should move smoothly with no notches.
Adjusting: tighten the top thread to 27 N·m, turn lock to lock, loosen it fully, then tighten it fully by hand.
Tighten the stem nut to 88 N·m.
checks: Stem top thread 27 N·m initial, then hand tight; stem lock nut 88 N·m (3-28)

VS sensor circuit malfunction — VS sensor or related wires
VS sensor malfunction — VS sensor or related wires; electromagnetic interference
Front pulser ring — pulser ring or related wires
Pump motor lock — pump motor (ABS modulator) or related wires; ABS MAIN fuse (20 A)
Pump motor stuck off — pump motor (ABS modulator) or related wires; ABS MAIN fuse (20 A)
Pump motor stuck on — pump motor (ABS modulator) or related wires; ABS MAIN fuse (20 A)
Power supply relay malfunction — power supply relay (ABS modulator) or related wires; ABS MAIN fuse (20 A)
Power circuit under voltage — input voltage (too low); ABS MAIN fuse (20 A); ABS SUB fuse (10 A)
Power circuit over voltage — input voltage (too high)
Tire malfunction — tire size; incorrect sprocket gear ratio (sprockets not recommended for the vehicle are installed)
ABS control unit — ABS control unit malfunction (ABS modulator)

pgmfi: Indonesia and Thailand bikes use these two-digit codes; Korea bikes use the P-codes below.
abs: A = detected in pre-start self-diagnosis; B = detected while riding. Erasing ABS codes without MCS: p. 4-57.
